KEY MESSAGE 1...Anomalously warm low-level thicknesses and
dewpoints beneath strong ridging aloft will continue to keep 
temperatures well above normal with potential record breaking 
heat continuing through Saturday, with heat index values 
peaking at 105-110 deg Friday for inland and nrn OBX zones, and
possibly again for srn zones on Saturday.

Friday continues to have the strongest signal for the peak of 
this week's heat wave, with highs ranging 95-100 for the
interior coastal plain, with low 90s coast. Thermal gradient
should be strong enough to allow for fast seabreeze progression
and thus preclude heat indices reaching 105 for immediate coast
outside nrn OBX, with HREF probs indicating this as well, but 
the combo of hot temps well above 90 inland coupled with TD's 
well into the 70s bring heat indices 105+ once again inland. 
Some locales may once again flirt with vals above 110 again, but
not long enough or widespread for issuance of heat warnings. 
HREF probs remain below 20%. 

Saturday a cold front will begin sinking in, but at the same
time TD vals inc with moisture gradient tightening ahead of it,
and with temps fcst to reach into the mid to possibly upper 90s
in swrn zones, another day of heat indices 105-110 degrees is
possible before expected numerous showers and storms ends the
heat later in the day. Best chances to reach criteria are
generally along and s of Hwy 70.

KEY MESSAGE 2...A strong upper level trough will develop off 
the U.S. East Coast over the weekend, and this will help drive a
strong cold front south through the Carolinas on Saturday. 
Strong heating of a moist boundary layer ahead of the front 
should allow strong instability to develop from the Mid-
Atlantic south into North Carolina on Friday. While some 
residual subsidence/capping may be present beneath the ridge, 
especially across NC, guidance show a decent signal for 
convection developing upstream of ENC, and making a run towards 
the nrn zones as early as late afternoon, but esp through the
evening hours. If convection can arrive early enough, severe
potential is there, esp north of Hwy 70 and best chances north
of Hwy 264. CAMs have generally inc in covg here, and thus
raised pops and thunder chances to likely after 22Z. Instability
is above the climo max for the first week of September, and
deep layer shear above 25 kt.

On Saturday, the ridge will continue to get suppressed further 
south and west with less influence across the Carolinas. This 
plus increased forcing along the cold front should support an 
improved risk of deep convection, and less limiting factors, 
compared to Friday. PW's/TD's inc further and with lowering hts
aloft, instability will be very strong. In fact, vals will be
well above the avg max for first week of September according to
the KMHX sounding climatology, with ML CAPE vals advertised by 
the 03/12Z RRFS/ECM/NAM3k reaching or exceeding 4,000 J/KG! If
convective timing aligns with fropa/shortwave passage in the
afternoon, a significant severe weather signal may be met as
this aligns with deep layer shear of 35-45kt. CSU severe probs
for damaging wind have increased to over 30% for parts of ENC 
and may suggest a higher risk than the current Day 3 'slight' 
risk from SPC if aforementioned parameters are met together.

In addition to the severe threat, will have to watch for
potential ff threat, as PW's surge to 2.25" or higher, and with
the expected numerous convection, very heavy rain rates are
possible with deeper convection and lend to instances of flash
flooding.

KEY MESSAGE 3...Behind the front, temperatures and humidity 
will finally get knocked down closer to normal for early 
September, with more comfortable conditions lasting into early 
next week. Still some residual moisture lingering on Sunday and
may see some sct showers, but overall trend is for drier esp as
we begin the work week with pops less than 20% lasting through
mid week. Highs in the mid 80s with lows in the 60s is fcst and
is where our temps should be for the first half of September.
